dialogues.speaker: Taruka
dialogues.text: No point trying to earn pity points with me. No means no.

choices.text: How are things? Getting along with Oberon?

response.speaker: Taruka
response.text: Come on, you, aiming your Saurian-chick eyes at someone else won't help you either. Just give up already.

response.speaker: Taruka
response.text: See, he's been like this ever since he got told to watch his diet. I'm doing this for his own good, you know... Hmm, that sounds like something Lamizana would say...

response.speaker: Taruka
response.text: A—Anyway, I'll adjust his diet whenever his flying performance gets back on track, or when he grows into an adult. Don't you worry!

response.speaker: Taruka
response.text: She and Lamizana are the same as ever, still real close and all... Bah, I don't get what she sees in him.

response.speaker: Taruka
response.text: But that's her decision to make, so I won't stop her. I've got my own concerns, after all.

response.speaker: Taruka
response.text: There's a lot I have to do before I can become the best adventurer in the Flower-Feather Clan.

response.speaker: Taruka
response.text: You've gotta become stronger with me, Oberon, or we won't be able to venture into Ochkanatlan together!

response.speaker: Taruka
response.text: You're leaving? Alright. You're welcome back any time.
